title: Coda Bassocyst
extract:
Coda Bassocyst is a unique Coda boombox shotgun that shoots wide sonic projectiles. Its Alternate Fire launches an Infested mite that latches onto enemy heads to inflict  Impact and  Magnetic status effects, while an enemy opened to a Parazon Mercy Finisher will perform a teleporting execution that strengthens damage and multishot.

Characteristics
This weapon primarily deals  Blast damage.
Performing a Mercy Kill grants +100% damage and Multishot for 20 seconds.
Primary Fire:
Innate Infinite Body Punch Through.
Projectiles have a thickness of ? meters.
Alternate Fire:
Launches a mite that latches up to 6 enemies, highlighting their heads for 5 seconds while dealing  Impact and  Magnetic damage and status effects per second for 10 seconds.
Consumes 4 ammo per shot.
Does not benefit from Multishot, neither in terms of total damage nor the number of hit enemies.
Has a large auto-aim cone (~90 degrees).
Does not trigger headshot conditions and does not benefit from headshot multipliers.
If the target is opened to a Mercy, the user will instead teleport to them and automatically perform a Mercy Finisher.
Bonuses stack additively with respective mods.
Buff duration is refreshed on Mercy kills.
Mercy Finisher needs a target under the teeth reticle, so to avoid unwanted teleports aiming above or below a target is a workaround.
Cannot be used without a target that is within 25 meters.
Projectile Speed mods like  Fatal Acceleration,  Galvanized Acceleration will extend this range.
Innate  polarity.
Adversary Weapon:
Comes with an additional bonus  Impact,  Heat,  Cold,  Electricity,  Toxin,  Magnetic, or  Radiation damage, which increases the listed base damage of the weapon by 25%-60%.
Valence Fusion can optionally change the resulting output damage type, and can upgrade the bonus increase (up to 60%).
Polarizing the weapon increases its max rank by 2, capping at rank 40 after 5 polarizations, granting the weapon additional mod capacity.
 Elemental Vice can be applied to the weapon after it has reached rank 40, allowing the bonus damage type to be swapped freely.
Unlike Kuva and Tenet weapons directly acquired from a Kuva Lich or Sisters of Parvos, the listed Mastery Rank requirement is enforced.

Acquisition

Coda Bassocyst is purchased from Eleanor of  The Hex in the Höllvania Central Mall for 10  Live Heartcell obtained from vanquishing a Technocyte Coda. Each offering has a random progenitor bonus damage type and percentage increase, which is cycled every 4 days.

Notes

Adversary Notes
For weapons obtained from vanquishing the Kuva Lich or Sister:
The player does not have to meet the Mastery Rank displayed to obtain this weapon. It can simply be claimed from the foundry after the Lich/Sister carrying it has been vanquished.
The weapon will have a prefix of the name of the Lich/Sister it was acquired from (e.g. a Kuva Kohm might be called "Odizrigg Agekk Kuva Kohm").
Refraining from Mercy killing an Adversary candidate and letting them die will remove their weapon from the pool of potential Adversary weapons until each has been refused, but only if the mission is completed. Weapons rejected from aborted missions will remain in the current cycle.
It is also possible for the weapon to be removed from the cycle even without waiting for the Adversary candidate to die before extracting from the mission.
For weapons obtained from Ergo Glast's and Eleanor's shop:
The player must meet the Mastery Rank displayed to obtain this weapon, as it is claimed from an NPC shop rather than the foundry.
The weapon's max rank caps at 40 after 5 polarizations (max rank increases by 2 per Forma added).
Additional polarizations can be added when the weapon reaches its new max rank at that polarization level.
Each additional rank also gives 100 Mastery Rank experience, giving 4,000 points in total at level 40.
Mod capacity scales with the additional ranks, and can reach a total of 80 at rank 40 with an Orokin Catalyst installed.
Without an Orokin Catalyst, the max is 40. Combined with the five polarized mod slots required to reach that point, an Orokin Catalyst might not be required for some beginner-friendly builds as they typically use less mod capacity.
After polarizing a weapon, any additional mod capacity above 30 (60 with an Orokin Catalyst) will not take effect until the weapon's rank reaches 31 and above.
Legendary Mastery Rank increases the minimum mod capacity for such weapons, without the weapon needing to be rank 31 and above. For example, Legendary 1 increases the minimum capacity to 31 (62 with an Orokin Catalyst).
Comes with an additional damage stat.
For Lich/Sister-obtained weapons this is dependent on the Warframe that summoned the Lich/Sister.
For Ergo Glast's and Eleanor's shops a random bonus stat will be offered for each weapon and changed every 4 days (96 hours).
This damage stat randomly ranges between 25%-60%. It can be upgraded up to its maximum value with Valence Fusion using another copy of the weapon.
The element of this bonus can be changed at will among the available Valence elements once an Elemental Vice is applied.
This bonus stat is considered a base damage type and will be applied after all elemental mods for the purposes of elemental combinations. It uses the weapon's falloff range but always scales linearly from 100% to 0%, regardless of what the weapon's falloff damage scaling is.

The reticle changes depending on whether your target is open for a Finisher.

Known Bugs
 Galvanized Savvy is multiplicative to base damage sources on direct hit, and does not affect the damage of the alt-fire.
Alt-fire doesn't interrupt  Prowl.
Alt-fire does not benefit from  Toxic Lash,  Resupply,  Seeking Talons,  Jet Stream or  Koumei's passive.
Universal weapon buffs such as  Xata's Whisper,  Nourish,  Valence Formation,  Shock Trooper,  Anabolic Pollination or  Theorem Demulcent do apply, with these buffs applying retroactively to mites already on targets.
Does not benefit from the damage multiplier of  Breach Surge, but does trigger sparks.
Every tick by the mite is affected by  Ballistic Battery and  Navigator, however only one mite will be affected.
Does not benefit from  Electric Shield, although this is likely due to not interacting with barriers, mentioned below in Coda_Bassocyst#Tips.
Mods or Arcanes that activate when a status effect is applied by a weapon (such as  Primary Blight,  Primary Exhilarate,  Shivering Contagion or  Magnetic Welt) do not trigger from status effects applied by the alt-fire.
Currently  Primary Obstruct and  Primary Debilitate are exceptions to this, working as intended with both forced and random statuses.
Status effects from  Primary Debilitate will still activate  Shivering Contagion as expected, as well as relevant arcanes on archguns.
If target dies or otherwise becomes an invalid target immediately before alt-fire would trigger a Mercy Finisher, the player teleports to the target without performing a Mercy Finisher.
Ragdolled enemies (such as those in  Strangledome) are valid for teleporting to but invalid for Mercy Finishers, allowing repeated teleports to the same target.

Tips
Has a unique buff lasting 20 seconds when a mercy kill is completed, granting 100% damage additive to mods such as  Serration and 100% additional multishot. This buff can be triggered with either the Coda Bassocyst's alternate fire execution, or doing a normal mercy kill without switching to it.
Alt-Fire ignores barriers created by Nullifier units and Arctic/Frozen/Cryonic Eximus units, but not the barriers around Guardian Eximus units. However, the projectiles can pass through a barrier from a Guardian Eximus to reach a different unit.
Alt-fire does not damage the body part the mite attaches to, instead damaging similarly to an ability. This is most visible when using  Xata's Whisper, resulting in bullet attractors typically on the lower torso or between the feet of the target.
Teleport from alt-fire can often fail to teleport, especially when enemies are on uneven ground or near walls. This is likely from failing to find a valid position to teleport the player, thus making this ability much less effective on certain tilesets.

Trivia
Has a unique reticle featuring "teeth."
The primary fire and alt fire have a base damage of 808 and 303 respectively. These are likely references to the Roland TR-808 drum machine and TB-303 bass synthesizer.
The magazine size and maximum ammo of 24 and 96 are likely references to audio as well. 24-bit, 96 kHz audio files, commonly referred to as 24/96, are among the most commonly distributed high-resolution audio formats.
The Coda Bassocyst's reload, like all Coda weapons, has a unique animation. Upon reloading, the Warframe feeds the gun by inserting more ammo into the gun's barrel, which it then 'eats' while the Warframe shakes their hand clean.
